newsitem.title: USA: Juror calls witness in U.S. airline bomb case.
newsitem.headline: Juror calls witness in U.S. airline bomb case.

text.p: By Gail Appleson, U.S. Law Correspondent
The trial of three militant Moslems accused of plotting to bomb U.S. passenger jets took a bizarre turn on Tuesday when it was disclosed that a juror telephoned a government witness over the weekend.

The contact, disclosed by the judge, caused a dilemma in the three-month old trial because it could have led the juror to be dismissed just days after deliberations began. Although the case could have continued with 11 jurors, prosecutors and defence lawyers decided to keep the female juror on the panel and deliberations resumed in late morning.

U.S. District Judge Kevin Duffy, who frequently warns jurors against talking to anyone about the case, said he was concerned because the juror failed to follow his instructions. He told lawyers the juror had obtained the phone number of the witness through her brother, who works at the same "very large corporation" as the witness.

Prosecutors said the witness who was contacted was Microsoft Corp. investigator David Swartzendruber, who walked jurors through key files taken from a laptop computer recovered from an apartment shared by two of the defendants.

The computer is considered key evidence against them because it contained flight schedules for the United, Northwest and Delta planes that were intended targets and detonation times for the planned explosions. It also contained a letter claiming responsibility for the bombings.

"To the best of my knowledge nothing happened," Duffy said of the conversation between the juror and the witness. He said he had been told that the juror told Swartzendruber "I can't talk to you about this case until after deliberations are over, but I want to talk to you about it afterwards."
Duffy said the witness informed the U.S. Attorney's Office after the call. He did not say whether the juror explained why she wanted to talk to the Microsoft expert.
The jury is not sequestered but their names and addresses are being kept secret. Duffy said the witness now knows the name of the juror who called him.

The trial, which began in May, involves charges that Ramzi Ahmed Yousef, Abdul Hakim Murad and Wali Khan Amin Shah plotted to bomb 12 airplanes last year in a bid to kill about 4,000 people flying to the United States from Asia.
